name: houthi

events.event: Iran announced a meeting between Iraq and Gulf countries in Oman on Monday to discuss the Strait of Hormuz.
Saudi Arabia shut its East-West oil pipeline on Friday following a drone attack.
Oman announced the postponement of the Iran-Gulf states meeting in Salalah.
Houthi forces launched attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia using dozens of ballistic missiles and drones on Sunday.
Iranian-backed Houthis captured the strategic island of Perim on Friday.
The Panama-flagged oil tanker El Gaia was struck by an Iranian missile last month and rendered inoperable.
At least one person was killed and four others wounded in an attack on an Iranian commercial vessel near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil prices rose more than 2% on Monday as fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Iranian strikes on vessels added to supply concerns.
The Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and the island of Perim inside the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
The US military rejected Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim that the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia struck a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz.
Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi announced the meeting was postponed 'in the interests of consensus'.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran had no problems with the UAE or other regional countries.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran's objection was directed at US military bases in the region.
Iran and Oman agreed to a temporary Hormuz shipping lane agreement.
Demonstrators in Syria burned tyres and blocked highways in cities including Hama, Khan Sheikhoun, and Maarat al-Numan.
Saudi Arabia's oil stocks at the Red Sea port of Yanbu could maintain exports for only five to seven days.
Houthi forces captured the port city of Mokha on the Red Sea coast last week.
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met with US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Jeddah.
Syrian parliament summoned Energy Minister Mohammed al-Bashir for a hearing on Thursday.
Syria's standing committee for the pricing of petroleum products issued a new temporary price list that took effect at midnight on Sunday.
Protests against fuel price increases spread across Syria for a second consecutive day on Monday.
Syria produces approximately 102,000 barrels of oil per day against domestic demand of around 325,000 barrels per day.
Major maintenance work at the Baniyas refinery in Tartus has reduced domestic refining capacity.
Donald Trump said he is open to negotiations to end the war with Iran.
The US spent an estimated $33.4bn on the war with Iran by 29 June, according to a Pentagon watchdog report.
Yemen's Houthis advanced on government strongholds in Marib and Taiz.
The government raised fuel prices by up to 40% for diesel and up to 28% for gasoline.
Saudi Arabia lifted all-clear alerts for the cities of Najran, Khamis Mushait, Jazan, and Abha on Monday.
The average national cost of a gallon of regular unleaded topped $4.31 on September 14, 2026.
Fighting between Yemen's Houthis and internationally recognised government forces worsened an already dire humanitarian and displacement crisis.
Bahrain announced it would not participate in the planned meeting between Iran and Gulf countries.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the meeting was a sign of Iran's good intention to promote regional security.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that an expected agreement with Oman would not trigger a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Brics leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026, expressing serious concern over the escalation in West Asia and calling for maximum restraint.
Escalating fighting along Yemen's western coast drove more than 2,000 Yemenis across the Red Sea to Djibouti.
The Houthis completed their takeover of Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline, capturing the port city of Mocha and the strategic island of Mayyun.
The Houthis are now positioned just 20 kilometres from the African coast and essentially control the strategically significant Bab al-Mandeb strait.
More than 2,000 people have fled Yemen to Djibouti over the past 24 hours, the International Organisation for Migration said.
India condemned an attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman.
India said 13 of the 14 Indian crew members onboard the MT El Gaia had been rescued.
Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed al-Nahyan met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described the proposed Hormuz meeting as an 'important event'.
US President Donald Trump said Iran 'wants to make a deal so bad' that 'they're calling constantly'.
Saudi authorities issued flood warnings urging residents to avoid valleys and low-lying areas.
Americans felt the squeeze from skyrocketing fuel prices, with gas rising 16 cents to a nationwide average of $4.31 per gallon.
All 50,000 U.S. personnel in the Middle East were placed on high alert.
Soldiers calling themselves the Armed Forces for the Restoration of the Homeland attacked Air Base 101, the presidential palace, and the national broadcaster in a coordinated assault.
About 200 Russian Africa Corps soldiers helped loyalist forces retake Air Base 101 by evening.
At least 27 people were killed and about 100 mutineers were arrested during the mutiny.
President Donald Trump suggested the United States could remain in Iran after the war and take control of its oil resources.
A vessel in the Strait of Hormuz was struck by a projectile, causing a fire and forcing its crew to evacuate.
Houthi forces deployed fighters to the Hanish islands, 100 miles north of the Bab el-Mandeb strait on Monday.
Saudi Arabia's oil production fell to 6.2 million barrels per day in August, its lowest level in 30 years.
Iran's foreign minister denied on Monday any involvement by Iran in the attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.
Iran's foreign minister accused the United States of producing false news regarding the pipeline attack.
At least 11 people were injured in an ammonia gas leak in Jordan's Aqaba industrial complex.
The southern port of Aqaba was evacuated as a precaution following reports of the gas leak.
The gas leak, which happened during maintenance work, was contained in the industrial complex.
Former CIA officer Scott Uehlinger said the US may be forced to intervene in the Red Sea.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it intercepted and destroyed an advanced MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz.
A Houthi projectile fell near the border with Yemen along the Red Sea, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings.
Brent crude rose $3.21 to $107.82 a barrel.
The Houthis hit civilian and economic sites in the cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jizan and Najran, injuring 73 people.
The Yemeni government's military launched airstrikes on Houthi positions in the port city of Mokha, the coastal town of Dhubab and elsewhere in Taiz province.
Iran's judiciary seized assets of 240 dissidents and journalists and froze 182 bank accounts.
Police Chief Ahmadreza Radan announced that more than 6,000 people had been arrested over the January protests.
Iran executed at least 532 people since January, including at least 29 in connection with the January protests.
Iran's judiciary made more than 2,000 inquiries to Iran's Central Bank regarding defendants' accounts.
Iranian authorities arrested three members of the Mojahedin-e Khalq (MEK) in an operation the previous night.
Security forces prevented the Chaharshanbe Suri fire festival from being used to trigger further unrest.
Houthi rebels seized the strategic islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish in the southern Red Sea.
Saudi Arabia sought military assistance from Donald Trump to help fight the Houthis.
The US provided only logistical and intelligence backing to Saudi Arabia.
Iran denounced Austria's refusal to issue visas to the Iranian nuclear chief for the IAEA General Conference.
Demonstrators in Hasakah and Deir ez-Zor blocked roads used by crude oil tankers and cut the al-Suway'iya bridge crossing between Syria and Iraq.
Residents in the city of al-Shahil blocked the road leading to the al-Omar oilfield, preventing tankers from passing.
Truck and haulage drivers in Raqqa staged a sit-in outside a grain storage centre, blocking the road to the silos.
Protesters in Idlib province blocked the M5 motorway near Maaret al-Numan.
A young man in Hasakah province attempted to set himself on fire in protest at price increases.
Energy Minister Mohammed al-Bashir stated that the price rise was needed to bridge a gap between the cost of importing petroleum products and their domestic selling prices.
The USS George Washington recently replaced the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East.
President Donald Trump admitted oil prices likely won't come down before the November 2026 midterm elections.
The Houthis have tightened their grip on islands in the Red Sea, giving them control over a vital global shipping route.
The Houthis have advanced down Yemen's Red Sea coast, raising questions about whether they can turn territorial gains into new revenue sources.
A video claiming to show Houthi rebels ambushing Saudi-backed mercenaries is actually footage of a 2024 Houthi military drill.
Regional officials stated that a crucial Saudi oil pipeline operated by Aramco would remain out of service for several weeks after being struck in a Houthi attack.
Iran's IRGC stated the tanker El Gaia was travelling along the southern route through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Panama canal plans to cut maritime traffic again due to worsening drought caused by El Niño.
The Panama canal plans to allow an average of 29.5 vessels to transit daily from October.
Saudi Arabia may have launched a Chinese-made DF-15A ballistic missile in Yemen.
Debris believed to be a DF-15A missile booster was found in Raghwan district of Marib Governorate.
Oil prices rose more than 1% on Tuesday as concerns over global supplies intensified.
Brent crude futures gained $1.24 to $106.93 a barrel on Tuesday.
US West Texas Intermediate crude futures climbed $1.29 to $102.65 a barrel on Tuesday.
US Central Command said the El Gaia tanker was hit again by an Iranian drone over the weekend.
A Pentagon watchdog report said the US spent an estimated $22.3bn on munitions during the first four months of its war with Iran.
The US suffered up to 30 MQ-9 Reaper drone losses, four F-15E fighter jets, and other aircraft during the war with Iran.
The US suffered significant equipment losses during a search-and-rescue operation in early April to recover an Air Force officer stranded in Iran.
The US incurred $113m in costs by early June, including the evacuation of American diplomats and citizens from the region.
Iranian attacks caused an estimated $184m in damage to US diplomatic facilities in Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.
Australian energy minister Chris Bowen said he would travel to Saudi Arabia next week to meet Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi will meet with Chinese counterpart Wang Yi in China on Wednesday.
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said on Tuesday that escalation is on the way in the region gripped by the Iran war.
The Arab Media Summit kicked off on Tuesday in Dubai with a wide array of regional leaders and officials.
